(1) we propose a dataset-internal, contrastive autoencoder for self-supervised pre-training on low-resource datasets; (2) we demonstrate that this approach is effective for zero, few, and supervised learning, even in low-resource settings; and (3) we provide empirical evidence that zero- and few-shot learning benefit from additional self-supervised training.
, for NLP tasks, the bitter lesson is that miniaturisation beats compute scale-up.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for text data, self-supervised learning from small, internal data can be as effective or more than self-supervising on external datasets.

, in the context of NLP 'text-to-text' tasks, self-supervised learning from 'dataset-internal’ sources can be a viable alternative to large-scale external sources, and can provide substantial performance gains in zero-shot and few-shot learning.

, in the future, we may be able to achieve state-of-the-art performance in zero and few-shot NLP tasks, by only using a small amount of labelled training data, and a small amount of unlabeled data for pretraining, without requiring massive amounts of external data, compute or pretraining.
